memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Anyone who touches them will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Anyone who touches them. The rule continues, unchanged, for the woman with the long illness.

Here is the question worth asking: did anyone still touch her?

The law made contact costly, not forbidden. Someone could still choose to sit with her, still bring her food, still hold her hand — and pay the price of a washing and an evening. The law set the cost. Love decided whether to pay it.

Every community has people whose situation makes closeness inconvenient. The widow whose grief has outlasted everyone's patience. The friend whose depression makes conversation heavy. The family member whose needs never seem to end. Nobody forbids us from drawing near. It simply costs something, so we drift.

But Scripture calls the church to be the place where people are not left alone. Carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ (Gal 6:2). Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: to look after orphans and widows in their distress (Jas 1:27).

Somebody in your life is waiting to see whether anyone thinks they are worth an evening.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who have you drifted away from because closeness became costly?
2. What would it cost you to move back towards them?
3. When has someone paid a cost to stay close to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, show me who I have quietly drifted away from. Give me a willing heart to pay the cost of staying close to people who need someone to stay. Amen.
